status: editorially-authored; awaiting automated and integrated QA

entries.definition: The details that identify where someone lives or where something is located; or to speak to someone or deal with a problem.
entries.definitionZh: 地址；称呼；向……讲话；处理（问题）
examples: Please write your home address on the form.
The manager addressed the team's concerns.
entries.tip: As a noun, the stress is usually on the first syllable; as a verb, it is usually on the second.
entries.breakdown: The noun identifies a location; the verb can mean speak to an audience or take action on an issue.
entries.related: location; residence; speak to; deal with

senses.definition: The details used to identify the location of a home, building, or other place.
senses.definitionZh: 用于确定住宅、建筑物或其他地点位置的信息。
examples: I changed my email address last month.
What is the address of the new library?

senses.definition: To speak to a person or group, often formally.
senses.definitionZh: 向某个人或群体讲话，通常较为正式。
examples: The principal addressed the students at assembly.
She addressed the audience before the performance.

senses.definition: To take action to deal with a question, problem, or situation.
senses.definitionZh: 采取行动处理某个问题、疑问或情况。
examples: We must address the safety concerns.
The report addresses several important issues.

entries.definition: The length of time that a person or thing has existed; or to become older over time.
entries.definitionZh: 年龄；年纪；时代；变老；老化
examples: What is the age of the building?
Some materials age better than others.
entries.tip: Use “at the age of” for a specific age. “Age” can also describe a historical period, as in the Stone Age.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a person's years, the time something has existed, or a long historical period.

senses.definition: The number of years that a person or animal has lived.
senses.definitionZh: 一个人或动物已经生活的年数；年龄。
examples: Children of the same age often share interests.
She started learning music at the age of six.

senses.definition: A particular period in history or a stage in the development of something.
senses.definitionZh: 历史上的某个时期，或某事物发展过程中的阶段。
examples: The Bronze Age followed the Stone Age.
We live in the digital age.

senses.definition: To become older or to change as time passes.
senses.definitionZh: 随着时间推移而变老或发生变化。
examples: Wine can improve as it ages.
The photograph has aged badly in the sunlight.

entries.definition: A quantity or total of something; or, in the phrase “amount to”, to be equal to or have the effect of something.
entries.definitionZh: 数量；总额；合计为；相当于
examples: We spent a large amount of money on repairs.
The small changes amount to a major improvement.
entries.tip: Use “amount” mainly with uncountable things; use “number” with countable items.
entries.breakdown: The noun refers to quantity; “amount to” is a common verb phrase meaning equal or add up to.

senses.definition: A quantity of something, especially something that is not counted as separate items.
senses.definitionZh: 某种事物的数量，尤指不按单个项目计数的事物。
examples: Add a small amount of salt.
The amount of information was overwhelming.

senses.definition: To add up to a particular total, or to have a particular meaning or effect.
senses.definitionZh: 总计达到某个数额，或实际上意味着、构成某种结果。
examples: The bills amount to more than one hundred dollars.
His actions amounted to a refusal.

entries.definition: A particular part of a place, surface, or subject; or the size of a surface measured in square units.
entries.definitionZh: 地区；区域；面积；领域
examples: This area is popular with tourists.
The room has an area of twenty square metres.
entries.tip: “Area” can refer to a physical location, a measured surface, or a subject of knowledge.
entries.breakdown: The context shows whether it means a place, a measurement, or a field of activity.

senses.definition: A particular part of a town, country, building, or other location.
senses.definitionZh: 城镇、国家、建筑物或其他地点中的某个区域。
examples: There are several cafés in this area.
The children played in a quiet area of the park.

senses.definition: The amount of space covered by a flat surface, measured in square units.
senses.definitionZh: 平面所占的空间大小，以平方单位计算；面积。
examples: Calculate the area of the triangle.
The garden has an area of fifty square metres.

senses.definition: A particular subject, skill, or part of someone's work or interest.
senses.definitionZh: 某个特定的学科、技能或工作与兴趣领域。
examples: Marketing is not my strongest area.
The course covers several areas of science.

entries.definition: A piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine, or website; an item or object; or a word such as “a”, “an”, or “the” in grammar.
entries.definitionZh: 文章；物品；条款；冠词
examples: I read an interesting article about wildlife.
In English, “a” and “the” are articles.
entries.tip: In grammar, English articles are “a”, “an”, and “the”. In publishing, an article is a written piece on a topic.
entries.breakdown: The meaning depends on whether the context is writing, grammar, law, or a general object.
entries.related: essay; report; item; a; an; the

senses.definition: A piece of writing about a subject, published in a newspaper, magazine, or online.
senses.definitionZh: 在报纸、杂志或网络上发表的关于某个主题的文章。
examples: She wrote an article about city transport.
I found the article on the school's website.

senses.definition: A word used before a noun to show whether it refers to something specific or general.
senses.definitionZh: 放在名词前，用来表示所指事物是特定还是泛指的词；冠词。
examples: “An” is used before a vowel sound.
The word “the” is a definite article.

senses.definition: An individual object or item, especially one of a group of things.
senses.definitionZh: 单独的一件物品，尤指一组物品中的一件。
examples: The shop sells household articles.
Each article must be labelled before storage.

entries.definition: The act of carefully watching, listening to, or thinking about something; or the interest and notice given to someone or something.
entries.definitionZh: 注意；留心；关注；照料
examples: Please pay attention to the instructions.
The new design attracted a lot of attention.
entries.tip: Common phrases include pay attention to, attract attention, and bring something to someone's attention.
entries.breakdown: Usually uncountable when referring to focus or interest; “attentions” has a different, more formal use.

senses.definition: The act of concentrating on something by watching, listening, or thinking carefully.
senses.definitionZh: 通过仔细观察、聆听或思考而集中精神；注意力。
examples: You need to give the speaker your full attention.
The child has difficulty keeping attention in class.

senses.definition: Interest or public notice given to a person, event, or subject.
senses.definitionZh: 人们对某个人、事件或主题表现出的兴趣或关注。
examples: The story received international attention.
Her bright jacket attracted attention.

entries.definition: A typical level or amount; the result of adding several numbers and dividing by how many there are; or to have a particular amount as a usual result.
entries.definitionZh: 平均数；平均的；普通的；平均达到
examples: The average score was eighty percent.
This town averages more rain in winter.
entries.tip: As a noun in mathematics, the average is commonly the arithmetic mean. As an adjective, it can mean typical or ordinary.
entries.breakdown: Can describe a mathematical value or something typical compared with others.

senses.definition: A number found by adding a group of numbers and dividing the total by the number of values.
senses.definitionZh: 将一组数字相加，再除以数字的个数所得出的数；平均数。
examples: The average of four and six is five.
Calculate the average of these test scores.

senses.definition: Typical or usual when compared with other people or things of the same kind.
senses.definitionZh: 与同类的人或事物相比，具有典型或通常水平的。
examples: The average adult needs regular sleep.
It was an average performance, not an excellent one.

senses.definition: To have a particular amount, rate, or result as the usual figure over a period of time.
senses.definitionZh: 在一段时间内通常达到某个数量、比率或结果。
examples: The team averages two goals per game.
The area averages a high temperature in July.

entries.definition: The part behind the main subject; a person's education, experience, or family history; or the conditions that help explain a situation.
entries.definitionZh: 背景；经历；出身；背景资料。
examples: The photo has a mountain in the background.
She has a background in graphic design.
entries.tip: “In the background” can mean physically behind something or happening without being the main focus.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a visual setting, personal experience, or information that explains a situation.

senses.definition: The part of a picture, scene, or place that is behind the main person or object.
senses.definitionZh: 图像、场景或地点中位于主要人物或物体后面的部分。
examples: A tree appears in the background of the photograph.
The singer stood in front of a blue background.

senses.definition: A person's education, family history, culture, or previous experience.
senses.definitionZh: 一个人的教育、家庭历史、文化或以往经历。
examples: Applicants should describe their educational background.
We come from different cultural backgrounds.

senses.definition: Information about earlier events or conditions that helps explain a situation.
senses.definitionZh: 有助于解释某种情况的先前事件或条件信息；背景资料。
examples: The report provides background to the decision.
I need some background information before the meeting.

entries.definition: The point at which something starts, or the first part of an event, period, story, or process.
entries.definitionZh: 开始；开端；起初；开头部分
examples: We are only at the beginning of the project.
Read the beginning of the story again.
entries.tip: Often used in “at the beginning of” and “from the beginning”. The verb is “begin”.
entries.breakdown: Refers to the starting point or earliest part of something.

senses.definition: The time or point when an event, activity, or process starts.
senses.definitionZh: 事件、活动或过程开始的时间或节点。
examples: At the beginning of the year, we set new goals.
The beginning of the meeting was delayed.

senses.definition: The first section of a story, book, period, or sequence.
senses.definitionZh: 故事、书籍、时期或顺序中的第一部分。
examples: The beginning of the film is quite funny.
I missed the beginning of the lesson.

entries.definition: A statement showing how much money is owed; a proposed law; a banknote; or to send someone a request for payment.
entries.definitionZh: 账单；法案；纸币；开账单；收费
examples: Could we have the bill, please?
The restaurant billed us for the extra meal.
entries.tip: In restaurants, “bill” is common in British English; “check” is more common in American English.
entries.breakdown: The meaning depends on the context: payment, government, money, or advertising.

senses.definition: A document or statement showing the amount of money that must be paid.
senses.definitionZh: 列明应付金额的文件或账单。
examples: The electricity bill arrived yesterday.
Can we have the bill after dessert?

senses.definition: A proposal for a new law that is discussed by a parliament or other law-making body.
senses.definitionZh: 由议会或其他立法机构讨论的法律提案；法案。
examples: The bill will be debated next week.
Members voted against the proposed bill.

senses.definition: To send someone a statement asking them to pay for goods or services.
senses.definitionZh: 向某人发送账单，要求其支付商品或服务费用。
examples: The hotel billed the company directly.
We will bill you at the end of the month.

entries.definition: A small piece or amount of something; an informal short period; or a unit of information in computing.
entries.definitionZh: 一点；少量；小块；短时间；比特
examples: Would you like a bit of cake?
Wait a bit and I will be ready.
entries.tip: “A bit” often means a little. In computing, a bit is the smallest basic unit of digital information.
entries.breakdown: A flexible informal word for a small amount, a short time, or a digital unit.

senses.definition: A small piece, part, or quantity of something.
senses.definitionZh: 某物的一小块、一部分或少量。
examples: He broke off a bit of chocolate.
There is a bit of water left in the bottle.

senses.definition: An informal word for a short period of time.
senses.definitionZh: 短时间；片刻。
examples: Stay here for a bit.
I will be back in a little bit.

senses.definition: A basic unit of digital information that can have a value of zero or one.
senses.definitionZh: 数字信息的基本单位，其值可以是零或一；比特。
examples: A byte contains eight bits.
The file stores one bit of information for each setting.

entries.definition: The lowest part of something; the surface or side underneath; or the lowest position in a ranking or list.
entries.definitionZh: 底部；底端；底层；最下面的；末位的
examples: Your shoes are at the bottom of the stairs.
The team finished at the bottom of the table.
entries.tip: Common phrases include at the bottom of, from top to bottom, and bottom line.
entries.breakdown: Usually identifies the lowest part or position, physically or figuratively.

senses.definition: The lowest part or end of an object, container, or place.
senses.definitionZh: 物体、容器或地点最低的部分或末端。
examples: There is a small hole at the bottom of the bag.
The village lies at the bottom of the hill.

senses.definition: The lowest position in a list, ranking, or situation.
senses.definitionZh: 名单、排名或某种情况中的最低位置。
examples: Our team was at the bottom of the league.
The price has reached the bottom of its range.

senses.definition: Located at the lowest part or end of something.
senses.definitionZh: 位于某物最下面部分或末端的。
examples: Open the bottom drawer.
The bottom shelf is easier for children to reach.

entries.definition: A plan for how money will be earned and spent; the amount of money available for a purpose; or to plan spending within that amount.
entries.definitionZh: 预算；经费；编制预算；经济型的
examples: We need to stay within our monthly budget.
They budgeted carefully for the trip.
entries.tip: Common phrases include on a budget, budget for something, and within budget.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a spending plan, the available amount of money, or the act of planning expenses.

senses.definition: A plan showing how money will be received and spent over a period of time.
senses.definitionZh: 说明一段时间内收入和支出安排的计划；预算。
examples: The school has a limited budget for new books.
We made a budget for our holiday.

senses.definition: To plan how much money can be spent and make sure spending stays within that limit.
senses.definitionZh: 规划可支出的金额，并确保花费不超过限额。
examples: You should budget for transport and food.
They budgeted carefully before buying a car.

senses.definition: Designed or sold to be relatively inexpensive.
senses.definitionZh: 为价格相对低廉而设计或销售的；经济型的。
examples: We stayed in a budget hotel.
The company offers a budget version of the device.

entries.definition: A person, event, or thing that makes something happen; a reason for a result; or to make something happen.
entries.definitionZh: 原因；起因；事业；导致；引起
examples: What was the cause of the delay?
Heavy rain caused the road to flood.
entries.tip: The noun “cause” often answers why something happened; the verb “cause” is followed by an effect.
entries.breakdown: Distinguish the reason for an event from the action of making that event happen.

senses.definition: The person, event, or condition that makes something happen.
senses.definitionZh: 促使某事发生的人、事件或条件；原因。
examples: The cause of the fire is still unknown.
Lack of sleep was the main cause of his tiredness.

senses.definition: An aim, belief, or organisation that people support because they think it is important.
senses.definitionZh: 人们认为重要并愿意支持的目标、信念或组织；事业。
examples: She works for a good cause.
The group raised money for the environmental cause.

senses.definition: To make something happen, especially something that produces a result or problem.
senses.definitionZh: 使某事发生，尤指造成某种结果或问题。
examples: The broken pipe caused serious damage.
His comment caused confusion.

entries.definition: The possibility that something may happen; an opportunity to do something; or to do something despite uncertainty.
entries.definitionZh: 机会；可能性；运气；冒险做某事
examples: There is a good chance of rain tomorrow.
This is your chance to ask a question.
entries.tip: Common phrases include by chance, take a chance, and have a chance of doing something.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to probability, an opportunity, or an action taken without certainty.

senses.definition: The likelihood or possibility that something will happen.
senses.definitionZh: 某事发生的可能性。
examples: There is a chance that the train will be late.
What are the chances of winning?

senses.definition: A suitable time or opportunity to do something.
senses.definitionZh: 做某事的合适时机或机会。
examples: I never had a chance to say goodbye.
She got a chance to study abroad.

senses.definition: To do or experience something when the result is uncertain, often involving risk.
senses.definitionZh: 在结果不确定时做某事或尝试某事，通常带有风险。
examples: I wouldn't chance driving in this storm.
He chanced upon an old friend at the market.

entries.definition: Communication with someone; a person you know who may help you; or to communicate with or touch someone or something.
entries.definitionZh: 联系；接触；联系人；联络；联系某人
examples: Please contact the office if you have any questions.
I keep in contact with my former classmates.
entries.tip: As a noun, “contact” often means communication or a person you can reach. As a verb, it means get in touch with someone.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to communication, a useful person, physical touching, or the act of getting in touch.

senses.definition: The act of communicating or keeping in touch with a person or organisation.
senses.definitionZh: 与某人或某个机构沟通或保持联系的行为。
examples: You can make contact by email.
We lost contact after graduation.

senses.definition: A person you know who may provide information, help, or an introduction.
senses.definitionZh: 可能提供信息、帮助或引荐的熟人；联系人。
examples: She has a contact at the travel agency.
I asked my business contacts for advice.

senses.definition: To communicate with someone by phone, email, message, or another method.
senses.definitionZh: 通过电话、电子邮件、消息或其他方式与某人联系。
examples: Please contact me when you arrive.
The school contacted every parent.

entries.definition: To say that something is true, often without having proved it; to ask officially for something you have a right to; or a statement that something is true.
entries.definitionZh: 声称；宣称；索取；索赔；主张
examples: He claims that he saw the accident.
You can claim a refund with the receipt.
entries.tip: A claim is an assertion or formal request. “Claim that” introduces a statement; “claim for” often relates to compensation.
entries.breakdown: Can describe an unproven statement, a request for something owed, or the statement itself.

senses.definition: To state that something is true, especially when it has not yet been proved.
senses.definitionZh: 表示某事属实，尤指尚未得到证实的说法。
examples: The company claims that its product is safer.
She claimed she had never met him.

senses.definition: To formally ask for money, property, or a benefit that you believe you have a right to receive.
senses.definitionZh: 正式要求获得自己认为有权得到的金钱、财产或福利。
examples: You can claim travel expenses from your employer.
He claimed a refund for the damaged item.

senses.definition: A statement that something is true, or a formal request for money or a right.
senses.definitionZh: 关于某事属实的陈述；或正式提出的金钱、权利请求。
examples: The report makes a surprising claim.
She submitted an insurance claim.

entries.definition: A group of students taught together; a lesson or course; a category of people or things; or a level of quality or social position.
entries.definitionZh: 班级；课程；类别；等级；社会阶层
examples: Our class starts at nine.
The museum has a large collection of objects from this class.
entries.tip: “Class” can refer to a school group, a lesson, a category, or social class. “Class” as a verb is less common and means to classify.
entries.breakdown: Its meaning depends on education, classification, social structure, or quality.

senses.definition: A group of students who learn together, or a period of teaching.
senses.definitionZh: 一起学习的一组学生；或一段授课时间。
examples: There are twenty students in my class.
We have an English class every Monday.

senses.definition: A group of people or things that share similar features.
senses.definitionZh: 具有相似特征的一组人或事物；类别。
examples: This class of machine is very reliable.
The library has a separate class for reference books.

senses.definition: A division of society based on economic or social position, or a level of quality.
senses.definitionZh: 根据经济或社会地位划分的社会群体；或质量等级。
examples: The novel explores differences between social classes.
She showed great class under pressure.

senses.definition: To place someone or something in a particular group or category.
senses.definitionZh: 将某人或某物归入特定群体或类别；分类。
examples: The material is classed as hazardous.
Researchers class the samples by age.

entries.definition: The state that a person or thing is in; a rule that must be met; or to train someone or prepare something for a particular situation.
entries.definitionZh: 状况；状态；条件；使适应；训练
examples: The car is in excellent condition.
You can borrow the book on one condition.
entries.tip: Common phrases include in good condition, on condition that, and under certain conditions.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a state, a requirement, or the process of preparing or training.

senses.definition: The physical or general state that a person, object, or place is in.
senses.definitionZh: 人、物品或地点所处的身体或总体状态。
examples: The house is still in good condition.
Her condition improved after treatment.

senses.definition: A rule, fact, or situation that must exist or be accepted for something else to happen.
senses.definitionZh: 某事发生前必须存在或接受的规则、事实或情况；条件。
examples: You can join on the condition that you follow the rules.
The offer is subject to certain conditions.

senses.definition: To train or prepare a person or animal, or to treat something so that it is suitable for use.
senses.definitionZh: 训练或使人、动物做好准备；或处理某物，使其适合使用。
examples: The athletes conditioned their bodies for the race.
Use a product to condition dry hair.

entries.definition: A link between people, places, ideas, or devices; a relationship or association; or a transport service that allows a journey to continue.
entries.definitionZh: 连接；联系；关系；转乘；接驳
examples: There is a strong connection between sleep and health.
We missed our train connection.
entries.tip: “Connection” can be physical, social, logical, digital, or related to travel.
entries.breakdown: The noun form of “connect”; it describes a link or relationship rather than the act of joining.

senses.definition: A relationship or association between people, things, ideas, or events.
senses.definitionZh: 人与人、事物、想法或事件之间的关系或关联。
examples: There is a connection between diet and health.
They discovered a connection between the two cases.

senses.definition: A physical or electronic link that allows devices, systems, or places to communicate or work together.
senses.definitionZh: 使设备、系统或地点能够通信或共同运作的实体或电子连接。
examples: Check the internet connection before the call.
The cable provides a connection to the monitor.

senses.definition: A service or route that allows a passenger to continue a journey by changing trains, buses, or planes.
senses.definitionZh: 乘客通过更换火车、巴士或飞机继续行程的接驳或转乘服务。
examples: We have a forty-minute connection in Singapore.
The airport connection was cancelled.
